answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity a slashable bond: each voter must lock collateral and earn signed receipts from already-bonded peers, who lose their own stake if they vouch for a twin. A clone posing as a pigment authenticator cannot inherit the original's receipts, so N fake voices need N separate bonds and N real endorsers. Caught duplicates are slashed, and the cost rises linearly whether the fraud hides on a mesa plateau or a remote ledge. Influence then tracks capital actually at risk, not the number of copies an attacker can spawn.
